newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan looks into N.Korean link to missing girl.
newsitem.headline: Japan looks into N.Korean link to missing girl.

text.p: The Japanese government is investigating a case of a school girl who may have been abducted and taken to North Korea 20 years ago, Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto said on Monday.
"Investigations by related authorities into the reported case is ongoing and the Japanese government is also working to collect information," Hashimoto told a parliamentary committee.
Hashimoto's remark was in response to a query about a report on the case in a Japanese daily newspaper.

The conservative Sankei Shimbun on Monday reported that South Korean security officials informed Japan of testimony by a North Korean defector who said he knew of a Japanese girl who was abducted 20 years ago.

The description of the girl by the North Korean defector closely resembled the case of Megumi Yokota, then 13, who went missing in 1977 on her way back from school in a coastal village in western Niigata prefecture, Sankei reported.
"I'm very surprised. There were various rumours (about her whereabouts) but I always had the feeling she was alive," said her father Shigeru Yokota.
Japanese security officials were quoted as saying it would be very difficult to prove whether the girl was alive in North Korea.
Reported abductions of Japanese by North Korea have clouded efforts to establish diplomatic relations between the two countries. Tokyo and Seoul established diplomatic ties in 1965.
In 1992, Tokyo and Pyongyang ceased normalisation talks when North Korea rejected Tokyo's demand for information about a Japanese woman it alleged was abducted by North Korean agents.

Kim Hyong-hui, a self-confessed North Korean spy who plotted to blow up a Korean Airlines Boeing 707 in 1987, said Yaeko Taguchi, who went missing in 1978, was the instructor who taught her Japanese language and customs working under the pseudonym Lee Un-hye.
